transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Um, yeah… I guess I’ve been having trouble with eating sometimes. It’s not, like, all the time or anything, but what really made me come in is that once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some kind of switch and I just keep going, even while part of me is thinking, “Dennis, just stop already.” I don’t know if that makes sense.
When you say you hit a switch and keep eating, does it feel like you’re losing control over your eating once it starts, like you can’t stop even if you want to?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but yes, that’s kind of what it feels like. Like once I’m in it, something flips, and even if I’m thinking, “Dennis, stop, you don’t need more,” I still keep eating. It’s embarrassing to say, but it does feel like I’m not really in control right then.
When you feel like you lose control while eating, does it usually happen all at once in a short period of time, like a binge where you eat a lot very quickly, or does it spread out more over the day?

It’s more like all at once, I think. Like… not the whole day of snacking or anything. Usually it’s at night, especially after a project deadline or if there’s leftover pizza in the apartment, and I’ll bring food to my room and it kind of happens fast.

I mean, it doesn’t sound great, but I might end up eating a whole small pizza, and then chips, and then cereal too. It’s definitely more than I meant to eat… probably more than my roommates would have for a normal dinner.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to compensate for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I feel bad afterward, but I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that. And I’m not, like, taking laxatives.

Exercise-wise… not really. I might think, “Okay, I should be better tomorrow,” but I don’t go do some huge workout to make up for it. Is that what you mean?
